summary: One player (Mind MGMT) secretly moves around a hidden map trying to recruit locations matching their feature cards while the rest of the team asks yes/no-style questions and cross-references clues on a shared deduction sheet to pinpoint and intercept them. It plays like a cooperative, more streamlined riff on Letters from Whitechapel/Scotland Yard, with a distinctive comic-book aesthetic and asymmetric roles.
praised: Tense, satisfying deduction puzzle for the hunting team
Strong asymmetry between the hidden-movement player and the deduction team
Attractive comic-inspired art and thematic integration with the Mind MGMT source material
Good scaling for a fully cooperative game, including solo/low-player-count variants
criticised: The Mind MGMT player's role can feel repetitive or less engaging than the deduction side
Some downtime for players waiting on questions/answers to resolve
Rules and bookkeeping (feature cards, immortals, tracking) have a learning curve
Replayability can dip once the map-reading and deduction patterns become familiar

interaction.kind: hidden movement and deduction via question-and-answer, one vs. team

scoring.why: The team wins or loses as a whole based on whether they corner and expose Mind MGMT before time/turns run out.
